suggestions.rationale: Mapping Expansion Batch ME-17 adds this relationship only as the user-approved bounded clinical proposition. The cited population-based twin study found strong co-occurrence between chronic widespread pain (the hallmark of fibromyalgia) and depressive and other psychiatric symptoms, with associations substantially mediated by shared genetic and family-environmental factors. Require independently established fibromyalgia or documented chronic widespread pain and a separately established depressive disorder; the cited population-based twin study found strong co-occurrence of chronic widespread pain with depressive symptoms, substantially mediated by shared genetic and family-environmental factors, and did not establish individual causation or direction. Preserve chronic fatigue, other functional somatic syndromes, musculoskeletal disorders, medications, substance use, and other psychiatric illness as competing explanations. Do not infer a depressive disorder from pain, fatigue, or impairment alone, and do not treat this population-level association as proof that fibromyalgia caused an individual's depressive disorder. The cited literature supports only this constrained proposition and does not, by itself, establish an individual medical nexus.
